title: A linear map preserving submodules induces a map of quotient modules, functorially
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$, $M'$, $M''$ $R$-modules with submodules $N\subseteq M$, $N'\subseteq M'$, $N''\subseteq M''$, and let $q:M\to M/N$, $q':M'\to M'/N'$, $q'':M''\to M''/N''$ be the quotient maps [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. (1) If $f:M\to M'$ is $R$-linear with $f(N)\subseteq N'$, there is a unique $R$-linear map $\bar f:M/N\to M'/N'$ with $\bar f\circ q=q'\circ f$, i.e. $\bar f(m+N)=f(m)+N'$. (2) If moreover $g:M'\to M''$ is $R$-linear with $g(N')\subseteq N''$, then $\overline{g\circ f}=\bar g\circ\bar f$; and $\overline{\mathrm{id}_M}=\mathrm{id}_{M/N}$.
